parts.text: Describe what happens from the moment a pollen grain lands on a stigma until a seed forms.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to four of the following:
• pollen tube grows down the style (1)
• to the ovary / through the micropyle into the ovule (1)
• male nucleus travels down the tube (1)
• fuses with the female nucleus / fertilisation (1)
• zygote develops into embryo and ovule becomes seed (1)

parts.text: Describe how an insect-pollinated flower is adapted for pollination.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• large coloured petals attract insects (1)
• scent (1)
• nectar as a reward (1)
• sticky / spiky pollen sticks to insects (1)
• anthers and stigma inside the flower (1)

parts.text: Describe how a wind-pollinated flower is adapted for pollination.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• anthers hang outside the flower (1)
• large amounts of light / smooth pollen (1)
• large feathery stigmas to catch pollen (1)
• small dull petals / no nectar (1)

parts.text: Describe how you would show that seeds need water to germinate.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to four of the following:
• set up two tubes of seeds on cotton wool (1)
• one tube kept moist, one dry (1)
• same temperature / oxygen / number of seeds (1)
• leave for a few days (1)
• count number germinated in each (1)

parts.text: Describe how a germinating seed obtains energy before its leaves appear.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• stored starch / lipid in the seed (1)
• digested by enzymes into glucose (1)
• glucose used in respiration (1)
• until the leaves can photosynthesise (1)

parts.text: Describe how a gardener could produce new plants by taking cuttings.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• cut a short stem with a few leaves from parent plant (1)
• dip cut end in rooting powder / hormone (1)
• place in moist compost (1)
• cover with polythene bag to reduce water loss (1)

parts.text: Describe the roles of oestrogen and progesterone in the menstrual cycle.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to four of the following:
• oestrogen causes the uterus lining to thicken / repair (1)
• oestrogen inhibits FSH / stimulates LH (1)
• progesterone maintains the uterus lining (1)

• progesterone inhibits FSH and LH (1)

• into fetal blood in villi (1)
• carried to fetus in umbilical vein (1)

parts.text: Explain why roughly equal numbers of boys and girls are born.

rows.answer:

• mother's eggs all carry X (1)

parts.text: Explain why height in humans shows continuous variation.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• controlled by many genes / polygenic (1)
• and affected by the environment / diet (1)

parts.text: Explain why two parents with brown eyes can have a child with blue eyes, where brown is dominant.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• both parents heterozygous / carry the blue allele (1)
• each passes on a recessive allele (1)
• child is homozygous recessive (1)

parts.text: Explain why a cross between red and white snapdragons produces only pink offspring.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• alleles are codominant (1)
• both alleles expressed in the heterozygote (1)

parts.text: Explain why the actual ratio of offspring from a genetic cross is often different from the predicted ratio.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• fertilisation is random (1)
• small number of offspring (1)

parts.text: Explain how a family pedigree can show that a condition is caused by a recessive allele.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• two unaffected parents have an affected child (1)
• parents must both be carriers / heterozygous (1)

parts.text: Explain why a test cross with a homozygous recessive organism can show the genotype of an organism with the dominant phenotype.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• if any offspring show the recessive phenotype the parent is heterozygous (1)
• if all offspring show the dominant phenotype the parent is probably homozygous dominant (1)
• recessive parent can only pass on recessive alleles (1)

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• seeds germinated increases up to 25 °C (1)
• then seeds germinated decreases (1)
• maximum of 90% at 25 °C (1)
• uses data, e.g. 4% at 5 °C and 8% at 40 °C (1)
rows.notes: Data quoted must include units

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• germination needs enzymes (1)
• enzymes break down stored food (1)
• low temperature: little kinetic energy / few collisions (1)
• high temperature: enzymes are denatured (1)
• optimum around 25 °C (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the percentage of resistant bacteria increased.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• resistant bacteria increases as years since antibiotic first used increases (1)
• then levels off / stays constant from about years since antibiotic first used 10 (1)
• uses data, e.g. 1% at years since antibiotic first used 0 and 50% at years since antibiotic first used 12 (1)
• rate of increase slows down (1)
rows.notes: Data quoted must include units

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• a mutation gives resistance (1)
• antibiotic kills non-resistant bacteria (1)
• resistant bacteria survive (1)
• resistant bacteria reproduce (1)
• pass on the resistance allele / gene (1)
• natural selection (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

• resistant bacteria increases as years since antibiotic first used increases (1)

rows.answer:

• a mutation gives resistance (1)
• antibiotic kills non-resistant bacteria (1)
• resistant bacteria survive (1)
• resistant bacteria reproduce (1)
• pass on the resistance allele / gene (1)
• natural selection (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

parts.text: Explain how natural selection could lead to moths with dark wings becoming more common in polluted areas.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to six of the following:
• variation in the population (1)
• caused by mutation / different alleles (1)
• competition / selection pressure, e.g. predation or food supply (1)
• individuals with the advantageous feature are more likely to survive (1)
• they reproduce (1)
• pass on the allele to offspring (1)
• allele becomes more common over many generations (1)
• this is evolution (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit any other valid biological points.

parts.text: Explain how bacteria in a hospital can become resistant to antibiotics and why this is a problem.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to six of the following:
• random mutation gives resistance (1)
• antibiotic kills non-resistant bacteria (1)
• resistant bacteria survive (1)
• and reproduce rapidly (1)
• pass on the resistance gene (1)
• population becomes mostly resistant (1)
• infections are hard to treat (1)
• overuse / not completing the course increases resistance (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit any other valid biological points.
